result.title: Improved Elastic Weight Consolidation as an Optimization Constraint for Continual Learning
result.summary: Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC) is a widely used regularization-based technique for continual learning, protecting performance on old tasks with a quadratic penalty whose empirical Fisher is usually justified through probabilistic curvature. We instead introduce Continual Learning as an Optimization Constraint (CLOC): new training must preserve chosen functionals of learned behavior. EWC's empirical Fisher is exactly the first-order form of this constraint when the preserved functional is each sample's loss. This derivation exposes a flaw: EWC implicitly weights each sample by the scale of its loss gradient, so well-fitted samples lose importance. EWC-DR observed this failure in classification; CLOC identifies its general cause. Improved Elastic Weight Consolidation (IEWC) penalizes output changes according to the first-order approximation of each old sample's loss level set, removing the weighting for any differentiable loss and output geometry, and prevents corrupt samples from dominating the importance matrix. Across classification, segmentation, language, forecasting, and diffusion, IEWC variants match or improve on EWC and outperform EWC-DR. In a held-out evaluation with validation-selected hyperparameters, uniform IEWC improves ImageNet-R accuracy over matched EWC by 2.00 percentage points (95% CI 0.93-3.07).

AI.brief_summary: 论文把持续学习表述为保持旧行为泛函的优化约束（CLOC），指出 EWC 的 Fisher 重要性隐含按样本损失梯度尺度加权，进而提出按每个旧样本损失水平集的一阶近似惩罚输出变化的 IEWC，并在分类、分割、语言、预测与扩散任务上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其以输出变化的一阶约束替代梯度尺度加权、避免部分样本主导重要性矩阵的思路，可能为 LVR 训练中保护既有推理行为或进行样本／参数贡献分配提供核查线索，但与 latent 状态生成无直接联系。
